subject: Post-demo playback: search fit & experiment plan for CypressBio
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@cypressbio.com>, Tom Evers <tom.evers@cypressbio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo playback: search fit & experiment plan for CypressBio

Thanks again for your time today — really helpful to see the notebook walkthrough and the three core search scenarios you outlined (literature lookup, protocol matching, internal SOP retrieval). Quick recap and a pragmatic experiment plan so we can confirm model fit and get you operationally confident: 

High-level recommendations (first pass)
- Retriever baseline: dual approach — initial BM25 index for deterministic recall checks + a semantic dense retriever (sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2) for production-like ranking.
- Reranker: use a lightweight cross-encoder (mini-cross-enc-bert or monoT5-small) for precision@1 tuning; fall back to a similarity-based ranker for latency-sensitive flows.
- Generator: evaluate two model families for hallucination/grounding: an instruction-tuned LLaMA-3-13B variant (quantized) and a smaller open instruction model we can run in your VPC for privacy-sensitive prompts.

Proposed 2-week probe (deliverables)
1) Controlled benchmark run: run our baseline prompt suite against a 500-query probe set (we'll provide prompts + golden answers). Measure precision@1, grounding-rate (percent of answers with verifiable citations), and hallucination incidents.
2) Retrieval ablation: BM25-only vs dense-only vs hybrid; measure recall@5 and grounding-rate on the same probe set.
3) Reranker A/B: cross-encoder (precision optimized) vs mono-similarity re-ranker (latency optimized) to quantify tradeoffs.
4) Prompt sensitivity matrix: short vs expanded context prompts + citation instructions to check regression risk when we tune for latency (e.g., smaller context windows).

Attachments: I attached the probe templates and the initial prompt suite (cypress_rag_probe_templates.xlsx, prompt_suite_v1.md). I also exported a CSV with baseline benchmark columns so your data team can map IDs.

Next steps (action owners)
- Cypress Bio: share a sanitized sample corpus (2-5k docs) or a representative metadata snapshot by Friday — Lena/Tom
- Redwood: seed the probe set, push an initial hybrid retriever run, and share a short benchmark deck by Tuesday — Aditya/Marissa
- Tech sync: 30m next Wednesday to review first run outputs and pick the reranker variant (invite to follow) — all

If that looks right I can kick off the probe and schedule the tech sync.

Best,
Aditya
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Park <lena.park@cypressbio.com>

Cc: Tom Evers <tom.evers@cypressbio.com>, Research AI Team <research-ai@cypressbio.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo playback: search fit & experiment plan for CypressBio

Thanks Aditya — this is exactly the kind of pragmatic plan we wanted. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Corpus: we can produce a redacted dump (~3k docs) but it will include mixed-length docs (abstracts, full protocols). Is your probe workflow OK with that variance?
2) Grounding definition: when you say "grounding-rate" do you mean presence of an explicit source in the top-3 results we used to synthesize the answer, or a weaker citation token? We prefer strict source attribution (link + doc id).
3) Latency targets: for interactive protocol retrieval, our bar is 400ms P95 for end-to-end (retrieval+rerank+gen). If cross-encoder pushes us over that, we may want a hybrid where cross-encoder runs only for high-confidence queries.

We'll start assembling the sanitized corpus and aim to share by Friday EOD. Also copying our infra lead (Tom) for any VPC/network constraints.

--
Lena Park
Head of Research AI, Cypress Bio
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@cypressbio.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo playback: search fit & experiment plan for CypressBio

Great questions, Lena — quick clarifications: 

- Corpus variance: yes, the probe harness handles variable doc lengths. We'll normalize passage chunking for the dense retriever and keep the original doc-level IDs so citations map back. We'll include a chunk->doc mapping in the exported CSV.
- Grounding-rate: agreed on strict attribution. For metrics we'll report both: strict attribution (exact doc id + paragraph) and loose attribution (document-level). The strict metric will be the primary signal for production readiness.
- Latency: understood. Proposed tradeoff: start with hybrid retriever + light cross-encoder (distil-cross) for the probe. If P95 > 400ms we'll evaluate a conditional reranker that only runs when dense-sim score is above a tuned threshold. We'll surface a latency/cost curve in the benchmark deck.

I've put the probe templates into the Drive link Aditya shared and added a sample mapping example. Tom — if you or your infra team need a signed MND before we load data into your VPC, say the word and we can route that.

Action: Aditya/Marissa to run the initial hybrid pass on a redacted subset as soon as we get the corpus.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Quick operational note and attachments:
- Attached: cypress_rag_probe_templates.xlsx (probe queries + golden-answer mapping), prompt_suite_v1.md (initial prompts with citation instructions), baseline-benchmarks-20270504.csv (benchmark columns schema).
- We'll run three permutations this week: BM25-only, Dense-only (mpnet), Hybrid + distil-cross reranker. Each run will produce a CSV with: query_id, top5_doc_ids, precision@1, grounding_strict (doc_id match), grounding_loose (doc-level), latency_ms_p95, reranker_time_ms.
- For the generator eval we'll keep temperature fixed and include 2 prompt variants (short / long). The idea is to detect quality regressions when we compress context.

Proposed tech sync: Wed 12 May, 09:00 PST — 30m. I'll send a calendar invite and attach the initial benchmark deck once the first run completes.

If you want us to prioritize a different reranker candidate (e.g., monoT5-large instead of distil-cross) call it out and we'll include it as an extra run (note: will add cost/latency).

Thanks — starting the orchestration now when you confirm corpus delivery.

-Aditya
